instruction: Run a speed test on speedtest.net and record the Download and Upload speeds in ~/Documents/bandwidth.txt, with each value labeled and on a separate line; create the directory if it doesn't exist.

metadata.explanation: This variation focuses on bandwidth-only data (Download and Upload) without requiring Ping metrics. It changes the output location to ~/Documents/bandwidth.txt. The task maintains similar complexity to the original - running speedtest.net and extracting specific results to a text file, but with a reduced metric set. Uses custom check_bandwidth_format__26660ad1 metric to verify proper formatting of Download and Upload speed values with numeric measurements.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Binary: 1.0 if file contains exactly 2 lines with proper format (Label Value Unit) for Download and Upload speeds, 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies all instruction requirements - file location (~/Documents/bandwidth.txt), presence of Download and Upload labels, proper formatting, and line count
Correct format validation: Metric function uses regex pattern '^(\w+)\s+([0-9]+\.?[0-9]*)\s+([\w/]+)$' to validate 'Label Value Unit' format exactly as required by instruction
Robust semantic verification: Validates exactly 2 lines, checks labels match expected order ['Download', 'Upload'], and verifies numeric values are valid floats
Correct expected parameter handling: Metric function correctly accesses expected_state['expected'] to retrieve the labels list, properly handling the rules dictionary returned by get_rule()
Practical feasibility: Getter can reliably extract file content from VM, no state timing issues since file persists after task completion
